subtitle: How Dasara’s Throne Became Mysore’s Public Stage

panels.shot: epic wide of a glittering durbar hall, golden throne at center, crowds receding into shadow
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits in full regalia on the golden throne in the Mysore durbar hall as rays of evening light fall on rows of courtiers and commoners gathered under high arches.

dialogue.text: In nineteenth‑century Mysore, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III and Chamaraja Wodeyar X turned the Dasara durbar into a public stage, where a watched king learned to rule by spectacle, music and shared ritual.

i18n.hi: उन्नीसवीं सदी के मैसूर में कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय और चामराजा वोडेयार दसवें ने दशहरा दरबार को ऐसा मंच बना दिया, जहाँ देखा जा रहा राजा तमाशे, संगीत और साझे अनुष्ठानों से राज सीखता था।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over Mysore town and palace complex at dawn
panels.action: A hazy morning view of early nineteenth‑century Mysore: the modest palace complex rises over tiled roofs and temple towers, with British officers’ bungalows visible at the edge of town.

dialogue.text: After Tipu Sultan fell in 1799, the old Wodeyar throne returned to Mysore, but under British eyes. A young Krishnaraja Wodeyar III grew up in a palace that was royal, yet closely watched.

i18n.hi: १७९९ में टीपू सुल्तान के गिरते ही पुराना वोडेयार सिंहासन वापस मैसूर आया, पर अब अंग्रेज़ों की निगरानी में। नौजवान कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय ऐसे महल में बड़ा हुआ जो शाही था, पर हरदम नजरबंद।

panels.shot: medium close-up of young Krishnaraja Wodeyar III with British resident in background
panels.action: A youthful Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, in simple royal attire, stands in a corridor holding a palm-leaf manuscript while a stiff British resident and staff stand in the shadowed background.

dialogue.text: He had power, but not sovereignty. Real decisions lay with the British resident and Dewans, yet the people still looked to the young king for signs that the old order had not died.

i18n.hi: उसके पास सत्ता थी, पर सम्प्रभुता नहीं। असली फैसले अंग्रेज़ रेज़िडेंट और दीवान करते, फिर भी लोग उसी जवान राजा में देखते रहे कि पुराना राजकाज अभी जिंदा है।

panels.shot: low-angle interior wide of Jagan Mohan Palace hall
panels.action: Inside the Jagan Mohan Palace, artisans erect a makeshift audience hall with draped canopies and a raised platform, while Krishnaraja Wodeyar III watches thoughtfully from a balcony.

dialogue.text: The Dasara festival, once shaped by Raja Wodeyar I at Srirangapatna, had lost its center in war and conquest. Krishnaraja Wodeyar III chose to rebuild it, not on a battlefield, but in a hall.

i18n.hi: राजा वोडेयार प्रथम ने श्रीरंगपट्टनम में गढ़ा हुआ दशहरा, युद्ध और फतहों में अपना केन्द्र खो चुका था। कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय ने ठाना, इसे रणभूमि नहीं, सभा‑भवन में फिर से जिंदा करेंगे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on durbar throne being polished and placed
panels.action: Palace attendants carefully position the golden throne on a low dais, polishing its carvings as priests sprinkle water and flower petals around it.

dialogue.text: From about 1805, the king’s Dasara durbar took new shape. The throne itself became a script: every ascent, every salute, every lamp and drumstroke telling Mysore that the Wodeyar line still lived.

i18n.hi: लगभग १८०५ से राजा का दशहरा दरबार नया रूप लेने लगा। खुद सिंहासन ही लिखावट बन गया – हर चढ़ाई, हर सलामी, हर दीप और नगाड़ा मैसूर को बताता कि वोडेयार वंश अब भी जिंदा है।

panels.shot: wide shot of durbar with clear division between elite and common spectators
panels.action: The durbar hall is filled: nobles and officials sit in ordered rows, while townsfolk stand along the sides and at the back, craning their necks to glimpse the king on his throne.

dialogue.text: This durbar was not closed. Doors opened to the town. Merchants, craftsmen and pilgrims stood beyond the nobles. The court, once a family ritual, now became a public grammar of kingship.

i18n.hi: यह दरबार बंद नहीं रहा। दरवाज़े शहर तक खुल गए। अमीरों के पीछे व्यापारी, कारीगर, यात्री खड़े होते। जो कभी घर का अनुष्ठान था, वही अब राज-पाट की सार्वजनिक पाठशाला बन गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III seated, musicians in foreground
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits upright on the throne, a serene smile on his face, while court musicians with veenas and mridangams sit cross-legged at the forefront of the hall.

dialogue.text: Music, too, was woven into rule. Under Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, palace halls became schools for veena and vocal art. In Dasara, these sounds framed the king’s body as calm, cultured and enduring.

i18n.hi: संगीत भी हुकूमत की बुनावट में घुल गया। कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय के राज में महल के सभागार वीणा और गायन की पाठशाला बन गए। दशहरे में यही सुर राजा के तन को शांत, संस्कारी और टिकाऊ रूप में गढ़ते।

panels.shot: close-up of an artist painting a genealogy scroll with the king nearby
panels.action: An artist kneels beside a long scroll, painting miniature portraits of earlier Wodeyar rulers, while Krishnaraja Wodeyar III looks on, one hand resting lightly on the edge of the scroll.

dialogue.text: In chancery and atelier, painters traced long genealogies, linking the boy king to centuries of ancestors. During Dasara, these images appeared in halls and pavilions, proof that this was no upstart court.

i18n.hi: दफ़्तरों और चित्रशालाओं में चित्रकारों ने लंबी वंशावलियाँ खींचीं, बाल‑राजा को सदियों पुराने पूर्वजों से जोड़ते हुए। दशहरे में ये चित्र हॉलों और मंडपों में सजे, दिखाते कि यह कोई नौसिखिया दरबार नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mysore streets with processions and British officers watching
panels.action: Festive processions with caparisoned elephants and torch-bearers pass through Mysore’s main street, while a small group of British officers watch from a verandah, arms folded.

dialogue.text: Outside the palace, Dasara processions threaded through town. British officers watched, amused or wary. For them it was color; for Mysoreans it was proof that their king still paraded the city as protector.

i18n.hi: महल के बाहर, दशहरा जलूस पूरे शहर में लहराते। अंग्रेज़ अफ़सर कभी हँसते, कभी चौकन्ने देखते। उनके लिए यह रंग तमाशा था; मैसूर वालों के लिए सबूत कि उनका राजा अब भी रक्षक बनकर शहर में निकलता है।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III in a study with books and instruments
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits in a small study lined with manuscripts and musical instruments, his face lit by a lamp as he writes on paper with a stylus.

dialogue.text: Within these ceremonies, the king himself changed. Krishnaraja Wodeyar III took to learning, composing, collecting. His palace became a place of books, instruments and measured ritual, not only of arms.

i18n.hi: इन रस्मों के बीच खुद राजा भी बदलता गया। कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय पढ़ने, रचने, संग्रह करने लगा। उसका महल तलवारों से ज्यादा किताबों, वाद्यों और नाप‑तौल वाले अनुष्ठानों का घर बन गया।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of durbar as a petitioning townsman speaks to a Dewan
panels.action: During a Dasara durbar, a modestly dressed townsman kneels before a Dewan seated below the throne, gesturing with a scroll in his hands as the king watches silently from above.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii_and_chamaraja_wodeyar_x
dialogue.text: Let them speak. A king who listens holds the city together.

i18n.hi: उन्हें बोलने दो। जो राजा सुनता है, वही शहर को जोड़े रखता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a later Dasara durbar, more crowded and orderly
panels.action: A later Dasara durbar shows a larger, more orderly hall with clearer rows for officials, guild representatives and townsmen, all facing the throne beneath a canopy of lights.

dialogue.text: Over decades, the durbar thickened. Petitions, honours and public announcements clustered around the throne. Ritual began to carry civic weight. The people saw not only a king, but a court that heard them.

i18n.hi: दशकों में दरबार गाढ़ा हो गया। अरज़ियाँ, सम्मान और जन‑घोषणाएँ सिंहासन के चारों ओर जुटने लगीं। रस्में अब नगर की ज़िम्मेदारी ढोने लगीं। लोग सिर्फ राजा नहीं, एक सुनने वाली अदालत भी देखने लगे।

panels.shot: transition shot: throne in shadow, young Chamaraja Wodeyar X in light
panels.action: The golden throne stands in semi-darkness while a young Chamaraja Wodeyar X, dressed in later nineteenth‑century attire, is lit by a shaft of light as he walks past it.

dialogue.text: Then, in 1881, another change. Chamaraja Wodeyar X returned to power in the Rendition, taking up a throne framed by British paramountcy and by a people now used to seeing their king in public ritual.

i18n.hi: फिर १८८१ में एक और मोड़। रेंडिशन के साथ चामराजा वोडेयार दसवें फिर गद्दी पर लौटे – ऐसा सिंहासन संभालते हुए जिसे एक ओर अंग्रेज़ी सरपरस्ती, और दूसरी ओर पब्लिक रस्मों के आदी हो चुके लोग घेर रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chamaraja Wodeyar X with Dewan and British official over a plan
panels.action: Chamaraja Wodeyar X stands at a table with his Dewan and a British official, studying a drawn plan of a council chamber while the outlines of a durbar hall loom in the background.

dialogue.text: Chamaraja did not undo spectacle. He balanced it. Alongside Dasara, he discussed councils, institutions and new schools, laying ground for representative bodies while keeping the durbar as a binding symbol.

i18n.hi: चामराजा ने तमाशा खत्म नहीं किया, उसे साधा। दशहरा के साथ‑साथ वह परिषदों, संस्थाओं और नए स्कूलों पर बात करने लगा, प्रतिनिधि निकायों की ज़मीन तैयार करते हुए, और दरबार को जोड़ने वाला प्रतीक बनाए रखते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Dasara durbar with signs of modernity: lamps, uniforms, order
panels.action: A late nineteenth‑century Dasara durbar glows with gas lamps; uniformed officials with files in hand stand beside turbaned nobles, while Chamaraja Wodeyar X sits on the throne under a canopy.

dialogue.text: The hall now held clerks with files and officers in new uniforms. Yet the rhythm remained familiar. Drums, lamps, the king’s ascent. Old ritual wrapped around new bureaucracy, making change seem continuous.

i18n.hi: अब हॉल में फाइलों वाले बाबू और नई وردी में अफ़सर भी थे। पर लय वही रही – नगाड़े, दीप, राजा की चढ़ाई। पुरानी रस्में नई अफ़सरी के गिर्द लिपट गईं, ताकि बदलाव भी लगातार लगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of townspeople from different walks of life watching the durbar
panels.action: In the gallery, a schoolteacher, a trader, a craftswoman and a young student stand side by side, watching the durbar below with mixed expressions of reverence and curiosity.

dialogue.text: By now, Dasara was Mysore’s common stage. Teachers, merchants, artisans and students all watched. They saw their own city reflected in the ranks below, and imagined a place for themselves in its order.

i18n.hi: अब तक दशहरा पूरे मैसूर का साझा मंच बन चुका था। गुरु, व्यापारी, कारीगर, छात्र सब देखते। उन्हें नीचे की कतारों में अपना ही शहर दिखता, और वे उसमें अपनी जगह सोचने लगते।

panels.shot: close-up on Chamaraja Wodeyar X’s contemplative face during durbar
panels.action: Chamaraja Wodeyar X sits on the throne, head slightly bowed, his face thoughtful as the murmur of the hall stretches out before him.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii_and_chamaraja_wodeyar_x
dialogue.text: These eyes judge not only a king, but a kingdom’s promises.

i18n.hi: ये निगाहें सिर्फ राजा नहीं, पूरी रियासत के वादों को तौलती हैं।

panels.shot: high-angle shot from behind the throne, looking out over the assembled hall
panels.action: From behind the throne, the vast assembly of the durbar hall stretches into the distance, rows of figures fading into shadow under the high ceiling.

dialogue.text: Under British oversight, with limited powers, the Wodeyars used what they still owned fully: image, ritual, and public time. The durbar became the frame through which Mysore imagined itself as a polity.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ी निगरानी और सीमित हकूमत के बीच, वोडेयारों ने वह पूरा-पूरा साधन साधा जो उनके पास बचा था – छवि, रस्म और सार्वजनिक समय। दरबार ही वह चौखटा बन गया जिससे मैसूर खुद को एक रियासत की तरह सोचने लगा।

panels.shot: wide twilight shot of Mysore Palace exterior during Dasara illumination
panels.action: At twilight, the Mysore Palace shines with rows of tiny lamps, crowds milling in the foreground while the silhouette of the throne room glows at the center.

dialogue.text: In the glow of Dasara lights, ritual and public life met. Krishnaraja Wodeyar III and Chamaraja Wodeyar X showed that a throne endures not by hiding, but by learning to let the people watch.

i18n.hi: दशहरा की रोशनी में रस्म और जन‑जीवन मिल गए। कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय और चामराजा वोडेयार दसवें ने दिखाया कि सिंहासन छुप कर नहीं, बल्कि लोगों को देखने देना सीख कर टिकता है।
